note: Known routable endpoints and their limits. Vendor facts, not user facts: which of these a deployment enables is its own choice (routing.use), and keys never live here. Every entry below was probed through fitroute's own adapter with json_mode on; `note` records what was measured and when. Limits marked 'published' come from the vendor's docs and are not independently verified. JSON rather than YAML because fitroute depends on stdlib + pydantic only, and because this file is intended to be machine-generated once discovery lands (DESIGN.md 8.15).

groq-llama70b.note: Measured 2026-08-06: json_mode VALID, 87 tokens. Most TPM headroom of the strong free models, which is what codegen needs - the rendered codegen prompt is ~6.4k tokens, so an 8k-TPM model has almost no room left for the generated file. Limits published.

groq-gptoss120b.note: Measured 2026-08-06: json_mode VALID, 223 tokens. Largest open model on Groq's free tier, but 8k TPM is tight against a 6.4k-token codegen prompt - listed after groq-llama70b for that reason, not for quality. Limits published.

groq-llama8b.note: Measured 2026-08-06: json_mode VALID, 87 tokens. 14.4k requests/day - by far the largest free daily budget measured, which makes it the right home for high-volume summarisation. Limits published.

groq-qwen27b.note: Measured 2026-08-06: json_mode VALID but 691 tokens for a trivial prompt - it emits reasoning traces, so it burns TPM far faster than its size suggests. Usable, but not a default. Limits published.

groq-compound-mini.note: Measured 2026-08-06: json_mode VALID, 589 tokens. 70k TPM is an order of magnitude above the rest, but it is an agentic system with built-in tool use rather than a plain model, so output is less predictable for structured codegen. Limits published.

gemini-flash.note: Measured 2026-08-06: json_mode VALID, 34 tokens. RPM measured (429 after ~6 rapid calls); RPD is a conservative guess - measuring it would cost a day's quota. Gemini emits no X-RateLimit headers, so limits cannot be learned from responses. Pro models are hard-blocked on the free tier at 'limit: 0' regardless of rate, so only the flash family is reachable without billing. trains_on_input: the free tier is the data-sharing tier.

gemini-flash-lite.note: Measured 2026-08-06: json_mode VALID, 40 tokens, 8/8 calls with no 429 - the most permissive Gemini model probed. gemini-3.5-flash was notably degraded the same day (one 503, 59s for 8 calls), so it is deliberately not listed.

openai-mini.note: NOT verified working. Probed 2026-08-06: the key authenticates and /v1/models returns 200, but every completion returns HTTP 429 'You have no credits remaining' - a zero balance, not a rate limit. structured_output is declared from vendor docs, not observed. Free tier limits (3 rpm / 50 rpd) require sharing prompts with OpenAI, hence trains_on_input.

ollama-local.note: Measured 2026-08-06: json_mode VALID, 54 tokens. Free, unmetered and private, so no rpm/rpd. Note fitroute has no reachability probe yet - a local entry is always considered credentialed, so a stopped Ollama fails at call time rather than being skipped (DESIGN.md 8.11).

ollama-coder.note: Measured 2026-08-06: json_mode VALID, 50 tokens. Worth recording that this is the model that produced prose for JSON-only prompts in 3 of 3 rogii campaigns; under constrained decoding it now returns valid JSON. That fixes the format, not the reasoning - it stays strong: false.
